title: Humanity-centered design: World Cleanupday Campaign
description: On my fifth semester UX-design and koncept development, my group and I developed a MVP for a campaign for the NGO Plastic Change, engageing kids to take action against plastic pollution, and come up with a way to generate revenue stream for the NGO.
imageCaptions: Sustainable Business Model Canvas for our concept
Sustainable UX Canvas for our concept
Side inviting sponsors to join the campaign, with focus on the value for the sponsor

sections.heading: Project description
sections.text: Focused on creating a sustainable and user-friendly solution for the NGO Plastic Change to create new revenue streams, with a focus on engaging more kids in the fight against plastic pollution. Our koncept re-thought sponsorship for the NGO, and proposed a more valueable and attacktive solution to sponsors.

sections.heading: Design choices for sustainability, revenue stream and engagement
sections.text: Even trough the users of the campaign where theachers and kids in 4,-9th grade, we designed the website for only teachers and sponsors. The side was two flows for signing up: as a educator that is planning a cleanup and as a new sponsor. A key point from the project was to make sponsorships more attractive for companies, and the business model build on them getting both advertisement and a certificate to share on LinkedIn. Secondly the sponsors also gained value from helping the envirement and their ESG's ratings

title: Design and develop page for Min Strøm app
description: Working with the head developer, owner and UX designer from the Min Strøm app, with over 500,000 downloads, my group redesigned and built a page for the app during our second semester.
imageCaptions: Min Strøm app today, the finished design with elements from our prototypes
Min Strøm prototype wireframes, used as a guide for development

sections.heading: The process
sections.text: Through conversations with the app team, user interviews and think-aloud tests facilitated by us, we improved the user journey. From the insights we collected, we made low-fidelity prototypes for the app team to evaluate. Through a few iterations, we developed our improved app in Kotlin Compose, the programming language for Android apps.

title: Designing to reduce waste in G James business process
description: My group worked with business analytics tools such as SWOT, TOWS, SIPOC, GAP analysis and BPMN, as well as stakeholder management, to find solutions to reduce waste in the giant warehouses and improve the company's digital maturity.
imageCaptions: Our timeline for digital maturity in the company factory

sections.heading: The project
sections.text: In my third semester, I worked with the Australian company G James, a manufacturing business specialising in the production of aluminium windows and doors, building facades, glass and aluminium extrusions.

sections.heading: Designing for a different context
sections.text: It was a fun challenge to design for a user group that was not English-speaking, but used many different languages, had limited reading skills and worked within a very different work culture from Denmark. We found that workplace norms such as not sharing opinions, not asking questions and a top-down approach with little employee involvement resulted in a slow feedback flow. Designing for users with low digital maturity was a very different and valuable learning experience.

title: Greenhouse Princess
subtitle: Personal project for fun - you can try soon (when i migrate backend so it can be used upsi)
description: Small site to keep track of your plants and their needs. Login to add plants and edit your own digital garden. Will soon be deployed for you to try!
imageCaptions: A plant page with all posts

sections.heading: The idea
sections.text: Greenhouse Princess is a vintage pixel art inspired website where the user can build a personal digital garden. Instead of listing plant information such as nickname, Latin name, care instructions and picture in a notes app, you can use Greenhouse Princess to keep it all together.
